exercises.name: Floor Crunch
exercises.muscle_targeting_notes: Trunk flexion or posterior pelvic tilt emphasizes the abdominal wall; hip flexors may assist, especially when legs move.
instructions: Lie or sit in a stable position with the pelvis and ribs controlled; use a small range first.
Curl the trunk or draw the pelvis toward the ribs without swinging; return slowly while keeping the neck relaxed.
Breathe steadily and use a pain-free range; do not hold your breath through the full set.
End the set when you can no longer keep the trunk and pelvis controlled.
common_mistakes: Using momentum or swinging the legs to complete repetitions.
Allowing the lower back to arch or round beyond a comfortable controlled range.
Pulling on the neck or shoulders during flexion movements.
Holding the breath or pushing through pain, pressure, numbness, or tingling.
safety_cautions: Stop for sharp or worsening back pain, numbness, tingling, dizziness, or unusual shortness of breath.
Choose a regression or smaller range if you cannot keep the trunk controlled; do not force end-range spinal flexion or extension.
Secure benches, bars, cables, bands, and suspension points; use a clear stable surface for floor work.
People with a current back, abdominal, or pelvic-floor condition or recent surgery should follow advice from a qualified clinician.

exercises.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
exercises.muscle_targeting_notes: Trunk and spinal muscles maintain or control position; use a comfortable range without forcing lumbar flexion or extension.
instructions: Set a neutral, comfortable spinal position and brace gently; use support or a shorter range if needed.
Extend or hold the trunk in a comfortable neutral position using the back and hip muscles; avoid forcing end-range arching.
Breathe steadily and use a pain-free range; do not hold your breath through the full set.
End the set when you can no longer keep the trunk and pelvis controlled.
common_mistakes: Using momentum or swinging the legs to complete repetitions.
Allowing the lower back to arch or round beyond a comfortable controlled range.
Pulling on the neck or shoulders during flexion movements.
Holding the breath or pushing through pain, pressure, numbness, or tingling.
safety_cautions: Stop for sharp or worsening back pain, numbness, tingling, dizziness, or unusual shortness of breath.
Choose a regression or smaller range if you cannot keep the trunk controlled; do not force end-range spinal flexion or extension.
Secure benches, bars, cables, bands, and suspension points; use a clear stable surface for floor work.
People with a current back, abdominal, or pelvic-floor condition or recent surgery should follow advice from a qualified clinician.
